jOOQ on The ORM Foundation? I am the creator of Spring-Data-OOJ, a full fledged implementation of jOOQ on the Spring-Data project. Spring-Data-OOJ can be translated to any Data Access API, not just Spring Data. It is meant to allow Data access independent of any storage back-end backend. Spring-Data-OOJ is under active development. You can use it right now in your projects. Note that it is in fact a prototype implementation, and with so many developers around the jOOQ community working hard to support the jOOQ spec, the current implementation has just a few small bugs left as well as some poor code readability. I am working on those right now. Spring-Data-OOJ support for the datastore management is incomplete and work in progress. This blog post will document which is the state of the prototype in relation to each milestone in the jOOQ WorkTrack project.

Support of jOOQ specification

The current implementation allows the creation of javax.persistence.EntityManager objects and execute query statements against them. It also supports the javax.persistence.Persisten’ence concept. For queries the BytecodeEmitter is stepping in to support inheritance analysis (which also works correctly in case of non-injectable objects in the jOOQ context). It also supports Hibernate-style annotations, but there is no support for MySQL-specific features. As of this writing these are called “Spring-Data”
